account: Be My AI is the image-description feature of the Be My Eyes app, and it runs on a large multimodal model. It was publicly released on 25 September 2023. Xie and colleagues at Pennsylvania State University analyzed image descriptions gathered in a social-media collection window from that day to 31 March 2024. They also interviewed 14 visually impaired users of Be My AI. In October 2024 Adnin and Das at Northeastern University reported at ASSETS that 19 blind participants in their interview study used ChatGPT and Be My AI in their everyday practices. A separate interview study of 21 participants, run from November 2024 to January 2025 and published at ASSETS 2025, records P9 using Be My AI to read a handwritten check. The paper by Xie and colleagues appeared at CHI 2025 and records individual uses. It reports that “P2 utilized it to identify gate numbers at the airport” and that “P10 used it to recognize her surroundings when disoriented in her neighborhood”. P13 received a description that located “a hair tie in the upper right hand corner” of a carpet. The interview participants' uses are undated, and the participants report the outcomes themselves. On 30 September 2026 Brigham and Kohno reported that low-star app reviews of Be My Eyes complain of inaccurate descriptions and paternalistic guardrails, and they name hallucinations as a problem with Be My AI.

ai_role.statement: The multimodal model generated the descriptions participants acted on. No independent per-task accuracy check was made. Participants themselves reported risk (P9: “I knew there was a risk”).

fields.account: Be My AI is the image-description feature of the Be My Eyes app, and it runs on a large multimodal model. It was publicly released on 25 September 2023. Xie and colleagues at Pennsylvania State University analyzed image descriptions gathered in a social-media collection window from that day to 31 March 2024. They also interviewed 14 visually impaired users of Be My AI. In October 2024 Adnin and Das at Northeastern University reported at ASSETS that 19 blind participants in their interview study used ChatGPT and Be My AI in their everyday practices. A separate interview study of 21 participants, run from November 2024 to January 2025 and published at ASSETS 2025, records P9 using Be My AI to read a handwritten check. The paper by Xie and colleagues appeared at CHI 2025 and records individual uses. It reports that “P2 utilized it to identify gate numbers at the airport” and that “P10 used it to recognize her surroundings when disoriented in her neighborhood”. P13 received a description that located “a hair tie in the upper right hand corner” of a carpet. The interview participants' uses are undated, and the participants report the outcomes themselves. On 30 September 2026 Brigham and Kohno reported that low-star app reviews of Be My Eyes complain of inaccurate descriptions and paternalistic guardrails, and they name hallucinations as a problem with Be My AI.
fields.summary: Blind and low-vision users of Be My AI, the GPT-4 image-description feature of the Be My Eyes app, report in peer-reviewed studies that it read airport gate numbers and a handwritten check.

purpose: Be My AI was built to describe photographed scenes and objects to blind and low-vision users. These task completions were that purpose. Xie et al. state that Be My AI is built on OpenAI's GPT-4 models.

ratings.reason: Participants who are identified by number report that they identified airport gate numbers, recognized their surroundings, located a dropped hair tie and read a check on their own. The results are small and self-reported, and the authors of the same papers document frequent errors.
